claim: Activating mutations involving the PI3K pathway occur frequently in human cancers.
source: Activating mutations involving the PI3K pathway occur frequently in human cancers.
evidence: This is a general statement about PI3K pathway mutations in cancer, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: PI3K inhibitors primarily induce cell cycle arrest.
source: However, PI3K inhibitors primarily induce cell cycle arrest, leaving a significant reservoir of tumor cells that may acquire or exhibit resistance.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section referencing prior work.

claim: A genome scale shRNA-based apoptosis screen was conducted in a PIK3CA mutant human breast cancer cell.
source: We searched for genes that are required for the survival of PI3K mutant cancer cells in the presence of PI3K inhibition by conducting a genome scale shRNA-based apoptosis screen in a PIK3CA mutant human breast cancer cell.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Five genes (PIM2, ZAK, TACC1, ZFR, ZNF565) were identified whose suppression induced cell death upon PI3K inhibition.
source: We identified 5 genes (PIM2, ZAK, TACC1, ZFR, ZNF565) whose suppression induced cell death upon PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screen described in the manuscript, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Small molecule inhibitors of the PIM2 and ZAK kinases synergize with PI3K inhibition.
source: We showed that small molecule inhibitors of the PIM2 and ZAK kinases synergize with PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Suppressing the 5 identified genes with PI3K inhibition induced tumor regression in vivo.
source: In addition, using a microscale implementable device to deliver either siRNAs or small molecule inhibitors in vivo, we showed that suppressing these 5 genes with PI3K inhibition induced tumor regression.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is frequently activated in breast cancers due to amplification of ERBB2.
source: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is frequently activated in breast cancers due to (i) amplification of ERBB2, an oncogene that stimulates the PI3K pathway and (ii) activating mutations of the PI3K catalytic subunit, PIK3CA (Koboldt et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Koboldt et al., 2012.

claim: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is frequently activated in breast cancers due to activating mutations of the PI3K catalytic subunit, PIK3CA.
source: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is frequently activated in breast cancers due to (i) amplification of ERBB2, an oncogene that stimulates the PI3K pathway and (ii) activating mutations of the PI3K catalytic subunit, PIK3CA (Koboldt et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Koboldt et al., 2012.

claim: ERBB2 is an oncogene that stimulates the PI3K pathway.
source: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is frequently activated in breast cancers due to (i) amplification of ERBB2, an oncogene that stimulates the PI3K pathway and (ii) activating mutations of the PI3K catalytic subunit, PIK3CA (Koboldt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ERBB2 function.

claim: Constitutive PI3K pathway activation promotes cell proliferation and survival.
source: Constitutive PI3K pathway activation promotes cell proliferation and survival, and previous reports have demonstrated that tumors harboring mutations that activate the PI3K pathway require constitutive signaling of this pathway for tumor maintenance.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the context of prior reports mentioned.

claim: Tumors that harbor mutant PIK3CA alleles exhibit significant dependence on PIK3CA expression and activity.
source: Specifically, tumors that harbor mutant PIK3CA alleles exhibit significant dependence on PIK3CA expression and activity (Cheung et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2011; Samuels et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by three citations.

claim: Oncogenic activation of PIK3CA leads to intrinsic resistance of HER2-positive breast cancer cells to HER2 inhibition.
source: In addition, oncogenic activation of PIK3CA leads to intrinsic resistance of HER2-positive breast cancer cells to HER2 inhibition (Berns et al., 2007; Hanker et al., 2013), and is more frequently activated in patients that exhibit acquired resistance to HER2 inhibition (Chandarlapaty et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Berns et al., 2007 and Hanker et al., 2013.

claim: PIK3CA is more frequently activated in patients that exhibit acquired resistance to HER2 inhibition.
source: In addition, oncogenic activation of PIK3CA leads to intrinsic resistance of HER2-positive breast cancer cells to HER2 inhibition (Berns et al., 2007; Hanker et al., 2013), and is more frequently activated in patients that exhibit acquired resistance to HER2 inhibition (Chandarlapaty et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Chandarlapaty et al., 2012.

claim: Inhibition of the PI3K pathway often leads to proliferative arrest rather than cell death.
source: However, inhibition of the PI3K pathway often leads to proliferative arrest rather than cell death (Elkabets et al., 2013; Klempner et al., 2013; Serra et al., 2008) and to date has shown limited clinical benefit.
evidence: This statement is supported by three citations.

claim: PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitor therapy induced a partial response in 18–30% of patients whose tumors harbor PIK3CA and/or PTEN mutations.
source: Specifically, PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitor therapy induced a partial response in 18–30% of patients whose tumors harbor PIK3CA and/or PTEN mutations (Janku et al., 2014, 2013, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Janku et al., 2014, 2013, 2012.

claim: Combination therapy consisting of Trastuzumab and Buparlisib resulted in a 17% partial response.
source: Combination therapy consisting of Trastuzumab and Buparlisib, a PI3K inhibitor, resulted in a 17% partial response (Saura et al., 2014), and mTOR inhibition combined with aromatase inhibitors in patients with hormone-receptor positive advanced breast cancer showed extended progression-free survival (Baselga et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Saura et al., 2014.

claim: mTOR inhibition combined with aromatase inhibitors in patients with hormone-receptor positive advanced breast cancer showed extended progression-free survival.
source: Combination therapy consisting of Trastuzumab and Buparlisib, a PI3K inhibitor, resulted in a 17% partial response (Saura et al., 2014), and mTOR inhibition combined with aromatase inhibitors in patients with hormone-receptor positive advanced breast cancer showed extended progression-free survival (Baselga et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Baselga et al., 2012.

claim: MDA-MB-453 breast cancer cells harbor a PIK3CA H1047R mutation and ERBB2 amplification.
source: To identify genes whose suppression converts the cytostatic response to PI3K inhibition into a cytotoxic response, we performed a positive-selection genome scale shRNA screen (Figure 1A) using MDA-MB-453 breast cancer cells, which harbor a PIK3CA H1047R mutation and ERBB2 amplification.
evidence: This describes the genetic characteristics of the cell line used in the study.

claim: Treatment with the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 leads to a complete proliferation arrest in MDA-MB-453 cells.
source: Treatment with the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 leads to a complete proliferation arrest (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and suppression of AKT activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) with minimal basal- and PI3Ki-induced cell death (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment with the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 leads to suppression of AKT activity in MDA-MB-453 cells.
source: Treatment with the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 leads to a complete proliferation arrest (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and suppression of AKT activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) with minimal basal- and PI3Ki-induced cell death (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Treatment with the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 results in minimal basal- and PI3Ki-induced cell death in MDA-MB-453 cells.
source: Treatment with the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 leads to a complete proliferation arrest (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and suppression of AKT activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) with minimal basal- and PI3Ki-induced cell death (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D.

claim: Suppression of each of the five identified genes resulted in reduction in the proliferation rate of untreated cells by 2–4 fold as compared to control shRNAs.
source: Notably, although suppression of each of these genes resulted in reduction in the proliferation rate of untreated cells by 2–4 fold as compared to control shRNAs, we did not observe evidence of apoptosis as measured by cleaved PARP (Figure 1D), indicating that the screen identified genes that only affect cell survival in the presence of the PI3K inhibitor.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Suppression of the five identified genes does not induce apoptosis in the absence of PI3K inhibition.
source: Notably, although suppression of each of these genes resulted in reduction in the proliferation rate of untreated cells by 2–4 fold as compared to control shRNAs, we did not observe evidence of apoptosis as measured by cleaved PARP (Figure 1D), indicating that the screen identified genes that only affect cell survival in the presence of the PI3K inhibitor.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The screen identified genes that only affect cell survival in the presence of the PI3K inhibitor.
source: Notably, although suppression of each of these genes resulted in reduction in the proliferation rate of untreated cells by 2–4 fold as compared to control shRNAs, we did not observe evidence of apoptosis as measured by cleaved PARP (Figure 1D), indicating that the screen identified genes that only affect cell survival in the presence of the PI3K inhibitor.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Over-expression of PIM2, ZNF565, and TACC1 rescued the effect of endogenous gene suppression by their corresponding shRNAs.
source: Over-expression of PIM2, ZNF565, and TACC1 rescued the effect of endogenous gene suppression by their corresponding shRNAs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Over-expression of the kinase-inactive mutant of PIM2 (K61A) failed to rescue the suppression of endogenous PIM2.
source: We also found that over-expression of the kinase-inactive mutant of PIM2 (K61A) failed to rescue the suppression of endogenous PIM2, suggesting that the kinase activity of PIM2 is essential for preventing cell death following PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the rescue assay.

claim: The kinase activity of PIM2 is essential for preventing cell death following PI3K inhibition.
source: We also found that over-expression of the kinase-inactive mutant of PIM2 (K61A) failed to rescue the suppression of endogenous PIM2, suggesting that the kinase activity of PIM2 is essential for preventing cell death following PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is inferred from the failure of the kinase-inactive mutant to rescue the phenotype.

claim: Overexpression of ZAK reduced cell viability in a kinase-dependent manner, but independent of shRNA suppression or PI3K inhibition.
source: Overexpression of ZAK reduced cell viability in a kinase-dependent manner, but independent of shRNA suppression or PI3K inhibition (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that ZAK overexpression itself reduces cell fitness.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ZAK overexpression itself reduces cell fitness.
source: Overexpression of ZAK reduced cell viability in a kinase-dependent manner, but independent of shRNA suppression or PI3K inhibition (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that ZAK overexpression itself reduces cell fitness.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ZAK overexpression reduces viability independent of other perturbations.

claim: PIM2 and TACC1 over-expression partially interfered in the interaction between PI3K inhibition and suppression of the other genes.
source: These experiments revealed that PIM2 and TACC1 over-expression partially interfered in the interaction between PI3K inhibition and suppression of the other genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that PIM2 or TACC1 generally contribute to cell survival in the presence of PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: PIM2 or TACC1 generally contribute to cell survival in the presence of PI3K inhibition.
source: These experiments revealed that PIM2 and TACC1 over-expression partially interfered in the interaction between PI3K inhibition and suppression of the other genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that PIM2 or TACC1 generally contribute to cell survival in the presence of PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing cross-rescue effects.

claim: Combining inhibitors targeting ZAK (HYJ-2-129-6, HYJ-2-34-2, and TL-01–124) and PI3K resulted in a synergistic response and conversion of the GDC0941-induced proliferation arrest into cell death.
source: Combining inhibitors targeting ZAK (HYJ-2-129-6, HYJ-2-34-2, and TL-01–124) and PI3K resulted in a synergistic response and conversion of the GDC0941-induced proliferation arrest into cell death (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B–D.

claim: TL-02–082, an analog of TL-01–124 that does not bind ZAK, did not exhibit a synergistic interaction with GDC0941.
source: We also found that TL-02–082, an analog of TL-01–124 that does not bind ZAK, but otherwise has a similar kinase selectivity profile, did not exhibit a synergistic interaction with GDC0941 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2E and serves as a negative control.

claim: Co-inhibition of PIM2 (HTH-01–091, and HTH-02–096) together with PI3K resulted in a synergistic response and conversion into cell death.
source: Similarly, co-inhibition of PIM2 (HTH-01–091, and HTH-02–096) together with PI3K also resulted in a synergistic response and conversion into cell death (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F–G.

claim: Suppression of the five genes in HCC1954, T47D, and HCC1937 cell lines leads to apoptosis in the setting of PI3K inhibition.
source: Similar to the effects observed in MDA-MB-453 cells, we found that suppression of these five genes in each of these cell lines lead to apoptosis in the setting of PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Inhibition of PI3K in breast cancer cell lines that have a wild-type PI3K pathway (CAL-120 and MDA-MB-231) failed to affect cell proliferation.
source: In contrast to the proliferation inhibitory effect of PI3K inhibition on breast cancer cell lines with activated PI3K pathway, inhibition of PI3K in breast cancer cell lines that have a wild-type PI3K pathway (CAL-120 and MDA-MB-231) failed to affect cell proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In breast cancer cell lines with wild-type PI3K pathway, suppression of the five genes had no effect on cell proliferation or apoptosis when combined with PI3K inhibition.
source: In these cell lines, suppression of the five genes had no effect on cell proliferation or apoptosis when combined with PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The ovarian cancer cell line EFO-21 (PIK3CA amplified) exhibited similar response to that observed in breast cancer cell lines with oncogenic PI3K activation.
source: In addition to breast cancer cell lines, we also tested four additional non-breast cancer cell lines. The ovarian cancer cell line EFO-21 (PIK3CA amplified) exhibited similar response to that observed in breast cancer cell lines with oncogenic PI3K activation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The interactions between PI3K inhibition and suppression of the five candidate genes in breast cancer cell lines did not occur in the three tested GBM cell lines.
source: However, the interactions we observed between PI3K inhibition and suppression of the five candidate genes in breast cancer cell lines did not occur in the three tested GBM cell lines (all that harbor PTEN inactivation) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The response to PI3K inhibition can be modified by the suppression of the five identified genes only in the context of oncogenic PI3K pathway activation.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the response to PI3K inhibition can be modified by the suppression of the five identified genes only in the context of oncogenic PI3K pathway activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses observed in cell lines with and without oncogenic PI3K activation.

claim: The combination of ZAK or PIM2 inhibition and PI3K inhibition induced cell death at a synergistic manner in T47D, HCC1954, HCC1937, and SKBR3 cell lines.
source: In addition, we found that the combination of ZAK or PIM2 inhibition and PI3K inhibition also induced cell death at a synergistic manner in four additional cell lines: T47D, HCC1954, HCC1937, and SKBR3 (bearing PTEN deletion and ERBB2 amplification) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Suppression of all five genes modified the response to HER2 or AKT inhibition, similar to the observation with PIK3CA inhibition.
source: Suppression of all five genes modified the response to HER2 or AKT inhibition, similar to our observation with PIK3CA inhibition (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Suppression of the five identified genes combined with inhibition of PDK1 or mTOR modified the response to PDK1 or mTOR inhibitors.
source: Similarly, suppression of the five identified genes combined with inhibition of PDK1 (GSK2334470, 2.5 μM) or mTOR (Sirolimus, 10 nM) modified the response to PDK1 or mTOR inhibitors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: The observed synergy between these genes and PI3K pathway inhibition is not specific to the particular PI3K inhibitor (GDC0941) used in the screen.
source: These observations demonstrate that the observed synergy between these genes and PI3K pathway inhibition is not specific to the particular PI3K inhibitor (GDC0941) used in the screen.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that multiple PI3K pathway inhibitors show similar interactions.

claim: The beta isoform inhibitor failed to interact with the suppression of the five identified genes.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, the only inhibitor that failed to interact with the suppression of the five identified genes is the beta isoform inhibitor, thus suggesting that the alpha isoform, PIK3CA, is the major isoform that mediates the observed interactions.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The alpha isoform, PIK3CA, is the major isoform that mediates the observed interactions.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, the only inhibitor that failed to interact with the suppression of the five identified genes is the beta isoform inhibitor, thus suggesting that the alpha isoform, PIK3CA, is the major isoform that mediates the observed interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of isoform-specific inhibitors.

claim: Suppression of the five genes did not convert the cytostatic effect of either CDK4/6 inhibitor or ER antagonist into cytotoxicity.
source: In contrast to what we observed following PI3K inhibition, suppression of the five genes did not convert the cytostatic effect of either CDK4/6 inhibitor or ER antagonist into cytotoxicity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The genes identified in this screen are specific modifiers of PI3K pathway inhibition and do not non-specifically affect cells whose proliferation is attenuated by other mechanisms.
source: These observations indicate that the genes that we identified in this screen are specific modifiers of PI3K pathway inhibition and do not non-specifically affect cells whose proliferation is attenuated by other mechanisms.
evidence: This is inferred from the specificity of the interactions with PI3K inhibitors versus other cytostatic agents.

claim: BAD is a substrate of PIM2.
source: BAD, a BH3-only protein whose phosphorylation leads to its sequestration by 14-3-3 proteins, is a substrate of PIM2 (Danial, 2008; Yan et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Danial, 2008 and Yan et al., 2003.

claim: BAD phosphorylation was reduced following PIM2 suppression with either shRNAs or a small molecule PIM2 inhibitor.
source: To test this hypothesis, we first confirmed that BAD phosphorylation was reduced following PIM2 suppression with either shRNAs or a small molecule PIM2 inhibitor (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A–B.

claim: PIM2 suppression significantly increased overall mitochondrial priming.
source: Suppression of PIM2 significantly increased overall mitochondrial priming (Figure 5C), consistent with the observation that PIM2 suppression reduces the phosphorylation of BAD.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Suppression of any of the other four genes (besides PIM2) did not lead to an increase in mitochondrial priming level.
source: In contrast, suppression of any of the other four genes did not lead to an increase in mitochondrial priming level (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the mechanism of interaction between PIM2 and PI3K inhibition is unique among the five identified genes.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mechanism of interaction between PIM2 and PI3K inhibition is unique among the five identified genes.
source: In contrast, suppression of any of the other four genes did not lead to an increase in mitochondrial priming level (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the mechanism of interaction between PIM2 and PI3K inhibition is unique among the five identified genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects on mitochondrial priming.

claim: Suppression of PIM2 resulted in caspase 9 cleavage when combined with PI3K inhibition.
source: Supporting this mechanism of interaction, suppression of PIM2 resulted in caspase 9 cleavage (Figure 5D) when combined with PI3K inhibition, indicating the involvement of mitochondria depolarization in the observed cell death.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Caspase 9 cleavage indicates the involvement of mitochondria depolarization in the observed cell death.
source: Supporting this mechanism of interaction, suppression of PIM2 resulted in caspase 9 cleavage (Figure 5D) when combined with PI3K inhibition, indicating the involvement of mitochondria depolarization in the observed cell death.
evidence: This is inferred from the known role of caspase 9 in mitochondrial apoptosis pathways.

claim: Combining PI3K inhibition with any of the siRNAs targeting the five identified genes leads to a significant reduction in the density of intact nuclei in vivo compared to non-treated control mice.
source: However, combining PI3K inhibition with any of the siRNAs targeting the five identified genes lead to a significant reduction in the density of intact nuclei as compared to non-treated control mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: All siRNAs targeting the five identified genes combined with PI3K inhibition exhibited greater effect than expected with a Bliss value significantly smaller than 1.
source: All siRNAs targeting the five identified genes combined with PI3K inhibition exhibited greater effect then expected with a Bliss value significantly smaller than 1 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The combination of small molecule ZAK inhibitors and PI3K inhibition resulted in a significant increase in the percentage of apoptotic cells in vivo.
source: Similarly, we also tested the combined effect of small molecule ZAK inhibitors and PI3K inhibition, and found that the combination resulted in a significant increase in the percentage of apoptotic cells as evidenced by staining for cleaved-CASP3 (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Over-expression of PIM1 can rescue cells from lapatinib-induced apoptosis.
source: We previously showed that over-expression of PIM1 can similarly rescue cells from lapatinib-induced apoptosis (Moody et al., 2015), corroborating a role for PIM2 in promoting resistance to PI3K inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Moody et al., 2015.

claim: PIM and AKT inhibitors synergize in acute myeloid leukemia.
source: In addition, it has been shown that PIM and AKT inhibitors synergize in acute myeloid leukemia (Meja et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Meja et al., 2014.

claim: PIM2 promotes tumor survival mainly through phosphorylation of the pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein BAD, as well as through regulation of MYC activity, and Cap-dependent protein translation.
source: PIM2 promotes tumor survival mainly through phosphorylation of the pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein BAD, as well as through regulation of MYC activity, and Cap-dependent protein translation (Nawijn et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nawijn et al., 2011.

claim: AKT and the PIM family of proteins share several common substrates, including BAD.
source: Of note, AKT and the PIM family of proteins share several common substrates, including BAD, while also having a number of unique targets (Amaravadi and Thompson, 2005; Nawijn et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Amaravadi and Thompson, 2005 and Nawijn et al., 2011.

claim: Additional kinases such as PKA and p90RSK also regulate BAD by phosphorylation.
source: Additional kinases such as PKA and p90RSK, also regulate BAD by phosphorylation (Danial, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Danial, 2008.

claim: BAD phosphorylation integrates survival signals from the PI3K and MAPK pathways.
source: Accordingly, BAD phosphorylation was shown previously to integrate survival signals from the PI3K and MAPK pathways (She et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to She et al., 2005.

claim: TACC1 has been shown to enhance mammary tumor formation induced by heterozygous PTEN loss in vivo.
source: One of the other candidates identified in this screen, TACC1, has been shown to enhance mammary tumor formation induced by heterozygous PTEN loss in vivo and was shown to mediate cell survival following PI3K pathway inhibition induced by PTEN over expression (Cully et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cully et al., 2005.

claim: TACC1 was shown to mediate cell survival following PI3K pathway inhibition induced by PTEN over expression.
source: One of the other candidates identified in this screen, TACC1, has been shown to enhance mammary tumor formation induced by heterozygous PTEN loss in vivo and was shown to mediate cell survival following PI3K pathway inhibition induced by PTEN over expression (Cully et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cully et al., 2005.

claim: TACC1 interacts with Aurora A-chTOG complex at the spindle pole during metaphase.
source: TACC1 interacts with Aurora A-chTOG complex at the spindle pole during metaphase (Conte et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Conte et al., 2003.

claim: TACC1 localizes to the midzone spindle and the midbody together with Aurora B during anaphase and cytokinesis.
source: At later stages of M phase, during anaphase and cytokinesis, TACC1 localizes to the midzone spindle and the midbody together with Aurora B (Delaval et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Delaval et al., 2004.

claim: Suppression of TACC1 leads to formation of multipolar spindles and thus perturbs cell division.
source: Suppression of TACC1 leads to formation of multipolar spindles and thus perturbs cell division (Conte et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Conte et al., 2003.

claim: PI3K activity contributes to genomic stability by regulating spindle orientation and chromosomal segregation.
source: Notably, PI3K activity contributes to genomic stability by regulating spindle orientation and chromosomal segregation (Silió et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Silió et al., 2012.

claim: Combined suppression of TACC1 and PI3K may induce cell death by causing un-resolved spindle and chromosomal segregation defects.
source: These converging mechanisms suggest that combined suppression of TACC1 and PI3K may induce cell death by causing un-resolved spindle and chromosomal segregation defects.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the known functions of TACC1 and PI3K.

claim: ZAK is a MAPK kinase kinase (MAP3K) that transduces signals through JNK and p38.
source: ZAK is a MAPK kinase kinase (MAP3K) that transduces signals through JNK and p38, and is associated with activation of AP1 and NF-κB (Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2014.

claim: ZAK is up-regulated in several cancers including breast cancer.
source: ZAK is up-regulated in several cancers including breast cancer (Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2014.

claim: ZAK over-expression has been shown to promote in vivo transformation.
source: ZAK over-expression has been shown to promote in vivo transformation (Cho et al., 2004) and cell migration (Rey et al., 2016), and its suppression reduced proliferation (Liu et al., 2014) and β-catenin activity (Firestein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cho et al., 2004.

claim: ZAK over-expression has been shown to promote cell migration.
source: ZAK over-expression has been shown to promote in vivo transformation (Cho et al., 2004) and cell migration (Rey et al., 2016), and its suppression reduced proliferation (Liu et al., 2014) and β-catenin activity (Firestein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rey et al., 2016.

claim: ZAK suppression reduced proliferation.
source: ZAK over-expression has been shown to promote in vivo transformation (Cho et al., 2004) and cell migration (Rey et al., 2016), and its suppression reduced proliferation (Liu et al., 2014) and β-catenin activity (Firestein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2014.

claim: ZAK suppression reduced β-catenin activity.
source: ZAK over-expression has been shown to promote in vivo transformation (Cho et al., 2004) and cell migration (Rey et al., 2016), and its suppression reduced proliferation (Liu et al., 2014) and β-catenin activity (Firestein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Firestein et al., 2008.

claim: Growth-factor stimulation, specifically EGF stimulation, activates ZAK.
source: Growth-factor stimulation, specifically EGF stimulation, activates ZAK (Cho et al., 2004; Rey et al., 2016), which then contributes to the activation of ERK signaling (Vinayagam et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cho et al., 2004 and Rey et al., 2016.

claim: ZAK contributes to the activation of ERK signaling.
source: Growth-factor stimulation, specifically EGF stimulation, activates ZAK (Cho et al., 2004; Rey et al., 2016), which then contributes to the activation of ERK signaling (Vinayagam et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vinayagam et al., 2011.

claim: ZAK inhibition by Sorafinib causes cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma due to suppression of JNK activity.
source: In contrast, it was recently shown that ZAK inhibition by Sorafinib causes cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma due to suppression of JNK activity (Vin et al., 2014), which might explain why over-expression of exogenous ZAK lead to reduced viability.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vin et al., 2014.

claim: ZAK influences cell state in a context-dependent manner.
source: Taken together, these observations suggest that ZAK influences cell state in a context-dependent manner, and that ZAK can either promote or suppress cell proliferation.
evidence: This is inferred from the various and sometimes contradictory roles of ZAK reported in the literature.

claim: ZAK suppression induced cell death upon PI3K inhibition, indicating that ZAK-mediated signaling is essential for cell survival in the context of PI3K inhibition in breast cancer cell lines.
source: Here we have demonstrated that ZAK suppression induced cell death upon PI3K inhibition, indicating that ZAK-mediated signaling is essential for cell survival in the context of PI3K inhibition in breast cancer cell lines.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing synergy between ZAK suppression and PI3K inhibition.

claim: The five genes (PIM2, ZAK, TACC1, ZFR, ZNF565) are either amplified or their expression is up-regulated in 37% of breast cancer patients.
source: Although there is no reason to expect that these 5 genes would be altered in human cancers, analysis of breast cancer genome sequencing data collected by the TCGA project (http://www.cbioportal.org) reveals that the five genes are either amplified or their expression is up-regulated in 37% of breast cancer patients.
evidence: This is based on analysis of TCGA data.

claim: 57 genes met the significance threshold based on STARS and RIGER algorithms.
source: Based on these two algorithms, 57 genes met this significance threshold (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), of which 36 genes were called by both algorithms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and 1F.

claim: 36 genes were called by both STARS and RIGER algorithms.
source: Based on these two algorithms, 57 genes met this significance threshold (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), of which 36 genes were called by both algorithms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Suppressing none of the five candidates reduced phosphorylation at Ser473 of AKT.
source: In addition, to determine whether suppression of these candidates affected PI3K signaling, we assessed the consequences of suppressing these genes on AKT phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H) and found that suppressing none of these candidates reduced phosphorylation at Ser473 of AKT, indicating that the observed interaction with PI3K inhibition was not due to further inhibition of the pathway.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The observed interaction with PI3K inhibition was not due to further inhibition of the pathway.
source: In addition, to determine whether suppression of these candidates affected PI3K signaling, we assessed the consequences of suppressing these genes on AKT phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H) and found that suppressing none of these candidates reduced phosphorylation at Ser473 of AKT, indicating that the observed interaction with PI3K inhibition was not due to further inhibition of the pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect on AKT phosphorylation.

claim: Every shRNA targeting the identified genes induced PARP cleavage following treatment with GDC0941.
source: In contrast, every shRNAs targeting the identified genes induced PARP cleavage following treatment with GDC0941, indicating the induction of apoptosis.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Suppression of each of the five identified genes resulted in an increased percentage of cells with a sub-G1 DNA content in the presence of GDC0941 compared to control cells.
source: In consonance with the cleaved PARP observations, suppression of each of the five identified genes resulted in an increased percentage of cells with a sub-G1 DNA content in the presence of GDC0941 compared to control cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The observed effects were obtained using at least three different shRNAs containing different seed sequences.
source: As indicated above, the observed effects were obtained using at least three different shRNAs containing different seed sequences, which ensured that these effects were the consequence of on-target activity of the shRNAs, rather than off-target suppression due to miRNA effects mediated by seed sequences (Jackson et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental design to ensure on-target effects.

claim: Using at least three different shRNAs containing different seed sequences ensures that effects are the consequence of on-target activity rather than off-target suppression due to miRNA effects.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jackson et al., 2006 and represents a methodological principle.

claim: At least three synonymous mutations were introduced into the shRNA-targeted sequence to prevent the suppression of exogenously expressed ORFs by shRNAs.
source: To prevent the suppression of exogenously expressed ORFs by shRNAs, we introduced at least three synonymous mutations into the shRNA-targeted sequence (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for the rescue assay.

claim: Overexpression of ZFR failed to rescue ZFR suppression.
source: We found that overexpression of ZFR failed to rescue ZFR suppression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: HTH-01–091 and HTH-02–096 exhibited high potency for PIM2 inhibition in a biochemical assay.
source: Specifically, PIM2 scored high in a kinase selectivity assay for two compounds, HTH-01–091, and HTH-02–096, which also exhibited high potency for PIM2 inhibition in a biochemical assay (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by data in Supplementary file 3.

claim: The potency of HTH-01–091 and HTH-02–096 as PIM2 inhibitors is similar to their potency toward PIM1.
source: Of note, the potency of both of these compounds as PIM2 inhibitors is similar to their potency toward PIM1, in contrast to commercially available PIM inhibitors that have a strong preference for PIM1 inhibition.
evidence: This is based on biochemical assay data.

claim: Three compounds (TL-01–124, HYJ-2-129-6 and HYJ-2-34-2) exhibited high potency as ZAK inhibitors in a biochemical assay.
source: In a biochemical assay to determine IC50, three compounds exhibited high potency as ZAK inhibitors (TL-01–124, HYJ-2-129-6 and HYJ-2-34-2).
evidence: This is based on biochemical assay data.

claim: HCC1954, T47D, and HCC1937 cell lines show activation of the PI3K pathway through different mechanisms.
source: To confirm the relevance of the candidates in other cell lines, we suppressed these same five genes in three additional breast cancer cell lines, including HCC1954, T47D, and HCC1937, which growth arrest upon PI3K inhibition. Each of these cell lines show activation of the PI3K pathway through different mechanisms: ERBB2 amplification (HCC1954), PIK3CA amplification (HCC1937) or activating mutation (T47D, HCC1954), and PTEN loss (HCC1937).
evidence: This describes the genetic characteristics of the cell lines used.

claim: PI3K inhibition in cells with a wild-type PI3K pathway activated by growth factors can suppress proliferation.
source: We also found that although PI3K inhibition in cells with a wild-type PI3K pathway activated by growth factors can suppress proliferation, suppression of these five genes did not modify this response (Figure 3A; MCF10A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A for MCF10A cells.

claim: In MCF10A cells, suppression of the five genes did not modify the response to PI3K inhibition.
